headline: Recommended filing the OPEB trust fund report and seven financial update reports, and recommended holding the annual comprehensive financial report.
summary: The Chief Financial Officer presented the reports. Members discussed sewer reserves, the snow operations budget, and the Community Preservation Act. Members voted to recommend filing most reports and to recommend holding the annual comprehensive financial report.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 17, 2026 meeting 3-0.
Recommended filing the annual report on the Other Post Employment (OPEB) Trust Fund, 3-0.
Recommended holding the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the year ended June 30, 2025, 3-0.
Recommended filing the financial update for the period ending June 30, 2026, 3-0.
Recommended filing the financial update for the period ending on May 31, 2026, 3-0.
Recommended filing the financial update for the period ending April 30, 2026, 3-0.
Recommended filing the financial update for the period ending March 31, 2026, 3-0.
Recommended filing the financial update for the period ending Feb. 28, 2026, 3-0.
Recommended filing the financial update for the period ending Jan. 31, 2026, 3-0.
Recommended filing the financial update for the period ending Dec. 31, 2025, 3-0.

Important Notice: Please be aware our office has been notified of an ongoing scam 
involving the impersonation of city officials and departments. Scammers are fraudulently 
requesting payments be made for planning and zoning permits, as well as City Council 
petitions. All official emails regarding your petition will come exclusively from an 
@worcesterma.gov email address (such as clerk @worcesterma.gov), or via physical mail 
on the City of Worcester’s official letterhead. Any legitimate hearing letter will always 
include your specific application details, along with the scheduled hearing date, time, 
and location. The City of Worcester will never request payments via wire transfer.

Fund.
# 14a CC March 10, 2026
a.
In Committee April 14, 2026 - Held
Chairperson Councilor Mitra read the item and recognized the Chief Financial Officer, who 
provided an overview of the item.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed how OPEB funding 
affects the city’s bond ratings with the Chief Financial Officer.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who discussed how health insurance 
costs are split between the city and people who are part of the city’s pension retiree program, the 
service requirement to be eligible for the city’s OPEB, how the city accounts for increasing health 
insurance costs and paycheck deduction for new employees with the Chief Financial Officer.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra then discussed the retirement benefit coverage, whether the benefits 
would cover surviving spouses, the trustees of the OPEB Liability Trust Fund, the election process 
and the length of term for the trustees, the Pension Reserve Investment Trust (PRIT) and how the 
city’s OPEB trust fund compares to other municipalities with the Chief Financial Officer.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be filed. 
Recommend File on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
Transmitting the City’s Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) for the year

# 11.26A CM August 18, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra read the item and moved to take up the item collectively with items 
#4b through #4g.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized the Chief Financial Officer, who provided an overview 
of the items.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed how higher revenues 
and lower expenses affect free cash calculations in November and how red flags related to 
revenues and expenses are monitored, addressed and reported to City Council with the Chief 
Financial Officer.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Rosen, who discussed concerns related to 
decreased sewer reserves, the needs to increase the sewer reserves to match the city’s reserve 
policy, usage of general funds in case of emergency, why the city does not provide 
recommendation for dual tax rates, the considerations related to making the dual tax rates into 
single tax rate and the impact of the Community Preservation Act (CPA) on the city’s budget with 
the Chief Financial Officer.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed the MA Department 
of Revenue (DOR)’s data on property values and incomes and the median income of property 
owners compared to the median income of the city with the Chief Financial Officer.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra then discussed challenges related to how snow operations budget is 
determined, the city’s ability to carry deficit for snow operations budget into the next fiscal year , 
whether the CPA can be paid online and plans to include CPA in the tax bill with the Chief 
Financial Officer.
Chairperson Councilor Mitra moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be filed.
